name: Commit signature intent guard
summary: Require an explicit or configured cryptographic-signing intent for Git commits.
description: A deterministic Claude Code PreToolUse gate for Bash that recognizes direct Git commit commands and blocks explicit signature bypass, dynamic command shapes, or commits without -S when commit.gpgSign is not enabled.
risk_reason: This automatic gate requires an explicit or configured cryptographic-signing intent for Git commits; a false denial can interrupt legitimate work, but it does not execute the blocked action.
refuses: It does not create, import, select, trust, unlock, rotate, or verify a signing key.
It does not sign, commit, attest, push, or claim that a future signature will verify.
It does not infer intent from branch names, commit messages, environment variables, aliases, or prompt text.
It does not expose a project-controlled bypass or accept --no-gpg-sign.

entrypoints.purpose: Verify statically observable Git commit signing intent before allowing the commit command to execute.

operational.latency_reason: To require an explicit or configured cryptographic-signing intent for Git commits, the entrypoint may run a bounded local subprocess before returning.
